The core mechanism operates through a layered permutation structure: the quarterback sequentially calls numbers (s_1, s_2, ..., s_n), but only one (e.g., s_2) is the true play indicator. This creates a signal-to-noise ratio optimization where the observer must decode a hidden permutation. The system's robustness hinges on the unpredictability of the mask function m(n) = k, where k is the true play index. Failure occurs when the adversary can estimate m via pattern recognition or repeated observation. Adaptive indexing introduces a feedback loop: if A(t) exceeds a threshold, then c_i is updated to c_j where j ∈ {1,3} to prevent signal leakage. This dual-layered approach ensures that even if partial signal integrity is compromised, the system remains resilient due to its stochastic nature.
